# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis

## 1. Scope of Evidence
Only one artifact was provided: `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames / ~26.4 MB). No Suricata/IDS export or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory. All findings below are derived directly from packet-level analysis with `tshark`.

## 2. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (confirmed via DHCP option 12, NBNS registration, and Kerberos) |
| Windows AD domain | WIN11OFFICE (NetBIOS) / win11office.com (DNS) |
| Logged-in user account | **WIN11OFFICE\gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString: gwyatt`, realm `WIN11OFFICE.COM`) |

Host obtained its lease from DHCP server 10.1.21.1 (Cisco device, 00:04:c1:be:8c:d4) at capture start, then performed normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP activity against DC WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com (10.1.21.2) — consistent with a domain-joined enterprise workstation.

## 3. Infection Chain (chronological)

All times below are frame timestamps (UTC+4):

1. **03:04:05–03:04:49** — Normal user browsing: Google, Bing, MSN, Office, Microsoft telemetry — establishes baseline legitimate traffic and confirms real Chrome/Edge browser activity (browser-consistent JA3 hashes, e.g. `3886fd6f…`, `2e6c64f6…` to google.com/msn.com).
2. **03:04:49** — DNS query for `hiyter.com` — first anomalous domain, acts as an initial redirector/landing point.
3. **03:04:49–03:04:52** — DNS queries for `media.megafilehub4.lat` and `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` — fake file-hosting domains, TLS sessions opened (encrypted, payload content unrecoverable without keys) — consistent with the drive-by/fake-download delivery stage.
4. **03:05:34–03:05:47** — Browser (real Chrome/Edge user-agent, confirmed browser JA3) is directed to `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) and served an anti-bot/browser-fingerprinting HTML+JS gate at:
   - `GET /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
   - `POST /api/set_agent?...&agent=Chrome&act=log` (same, repeated for Edge UA)
   - The served script collects WebGL/Canvas/Audio/WebRTC fingerprints, screen/hardware/navigator properties, and exfiltrates them via `POST …&act=log`, then redirects to `about:blank`. (Server: `nginx/1.29.1`; page contains a Cyrillic code comment — `Преобразуем в URLSearchParams` — indicating a Russian-speaking operator.)
5. **03:05:38 onward** — A **separate, non-browser TLS client** (distinct JA3 `2800f914a7a4ba98aa9df62d316a460c`, cipher-suite order inconsistent with any browser on this host) begins repeatedly connecting to **whitepepper.su:443** — 14 short-lived TLS sessions over ~30 seconds, each moving 1.6–5.6 KB, i.e. periodic check-in/beacon behavior rather than page loads.
6. The **identical malicious JA3** (`2800f914…`) also connects to `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156), `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36), and `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24) — confirming a single implanted process (not the browser) is using these four domains as C2/redirector infrastructure behind common hosting (nginx/Cloudflare).

This sequence (fake-download TDS → browser/device fingerprinting gate with `id`/`token` bot identifiers → dedicated executable beaconing to the same infrastructure with a non-browser TLS stack) is the signature behavior of a **commodity loader/stealer delivered via a fake-download / anti-bot TDS (traffic-distribution-system) gate**.

## 4. Malware Family Attribution

**Attribution type: BEHAVIORAL, NOT signature-confirmed.**

No Suricata/YARA/AV artifacts were provided, and no payload binary was recoverable from the capture (all payload transfers occurred over TLS with no available decryption keys), so no hash- or signature-level identification is possible from this evidence alone.

Based on observed behavior — a fake-file-host delivery chain, a fingerprinting/anti-bot gate with `id`+`token` bot registration (`/api/set_agent`) and `act=log` telemetry exfil, followed by dedicated non-browser TLS beaconing to the same backend infrastructure across multiple throwaway domains — this traffic is **consistent with a commodity information-stealer/loader distributed through a fake-CAPTCHA/fake-download TDS** (the pattern commonly associated with Lumma-Stealer-style distribution networks). I am naming this the most likely family match, but flag it explicitly as an unconfirmed, behavior-based hypothesis — a definitive family name would require static analysis of the retrieved binary or a signature/YARA match, neither of which is possible from PCAP evidence alone.

## 5. Indicators of Compromise

### C2 / malicious endpoints (IP:port)
| IP:Port | Domain | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 153.92.1.49:443, 153.92.1.49:80 | whitepepper.su | Primary C2 — fingerprinting gate + repeated non-browser beacon (14 sessions) |
| 62.72.32.156:443 | whooptm.cyou | C2/redirector (same malicious JA3) |
| 104.21.9.36:443 | communicationfirewall-security.cc | C2/redirector (same malicious JA3, Cloudflare-fronted) |
| 80.97.160.24:443 | holiday-forever.cc | C2/redirector (same malicious JA3) |
| 104.21.48.156:443, 172.67.154.67 | media.megafilehub4.lat | Fake file-host, payload delivery stage |
| 104.21.46.67:443, 172.67.136.13 | arch.filemegahab4.sbs | Fake file-host, payload delivery stage |
| 104.21.22.231:443, 172.67.207.145 | hiyter.com | Initial redirector/landing domain |

### Malicious domains
- hiyter.com
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- whooptm.cyou
- whitepepper.su
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

### Malicious URLs
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

### Bot / campaign identifiers
- Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
- Token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Malicious TLS client fingerprint (non-browser process on victim host)
- JA3: `2800f914a7a4ba98aa9df62d316a460c` — observed against whitepepper.su, whooptm.cyou, communicationfirewall-security.cc, holiday-forever.cc. This JA3 does not match the host's genuine browser JA3s (e.g. `3886fd6f366b92455a2a260181321203`, `2e6c64f66822fc35b6a7a128b557f1de` seen on legitimate Google/MSN sessions), confirming the beacon traffic originates from an implanted executable, not the browser.

### Transferred files / hashes
No executable or binary payload was recoverable in cleartext. All payload/data transfers between the victim and the malicious infrastructure (megafilehub4.lat, filemegahab4.sbs, whitepepper.su, whooptm.cyou, communicationfirewall-security.cc, holiday-forever.cc) occurred over TLS 1.2/1.3 with no decryption keys present in the capture, so **no SHA256 hashes or filenames could be extracted from this evidence**. The only objects recoverable via HTTP object export were the benign NCSI test file, a Google time-sync JSON blob, `favicon.ico`, and the fingerprinting-gate HTML/JS pages listed above — no malware binary was served over cleartext HTTP.

## 6. Recommended Actions
- Isolate 10.1.21.58 (DESKTOP-ES9F3ML) from the network immediately.
- Reset credentials for WIN11OFFICE\gwyatt (stealer/loader activity implies possible credential exposure).
- Block outbound traffic to the 7 domains/IPs listed above at the perimeter firewall/DNS sinkhole.
- Acquire a memory/disk forensic image of the host to recover the dropped binary for static/hash analysis and definitive family attribution — this cannot be completed from network evidence alone.
